subject: Science
central_question: How do contact and non-contact forces change motion and shape, determine weight, and interact with liquids to produce floating or sinking?
in_scope_units: Force as a push or pull arising from interaction and its effects on motion and shape.
Contact forces: muscular force and friction, including surface dependence and fluid friction.
Non-contact magnetic, electrostatic and gravitational forces.
Weight, mass, spring balances, range, least count and measurement.
Buoyant force, Archimedes' principle, floating and sinking.
banned_topics: Detailed density calculations, taught in Chapter 9.

known_pitfalls.claim: An object at rest has no forces acting on it.
known_pitfalls.correction: Forces may act but balance one another, producing no change in motion.

known_pitfalls.claim: Friction always acts in the direction of motion.
known_pitfalls.correction: Friction opposes the direction in which an object moves or tries to move.

known_pitfalls.claim: Mass and weight are the same quantity.
known_pitfalls.correction: Mass is amount of matter in kg or g; weight is gravitational force in newtons and can vary by location.

known_pitfalls.claim: Gravity acts only on falling objects.
known_pitfalls.correction: Earth's gravitational force acts on objects continuously, including at the topmost point of a throw.

known_pitfalls.claim: A larger object must sink and a smaller object must float.
known_pitfalls.correction: Floating depends on the relationship between weight and buoyant force, not size alone.

recommended_example_progression: Use Activities 5.1 and 5.2 to define force and its effects.
Use Activities 5.3 and 5.4 to infer the direction and surface dependence of friction.
Use Activities 5.5–5.8 to compare non-contact forces.
Use Activities 5.9–5.12 to read and use a spring balance.
Use Activity 5.13 and Keep the curiosity alive Q4 and Q10 for buoyancy.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The end section Keep the curiosity alive contains Questions 1–10, followed by Discover, design, and debate projects.
